papers.titleEn: Interfacial Hydrophilization-Assisted Buried-Interface Reconstruction for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) stand out as competitive hole‐transport materials for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), benefiting from their low‐temperature processing and robust operational stability. Nevertheless, intrinsic SAM aggregation and surface hydrophobicity hinder perovskite precursor wetting, trigger uneven buried‐interface nucleation, and worsen interfacial contact, limiting device performance improvement. Herein, two fluorinated phosphonic‐acid molecules, namely FPA‐Ph and FPA‐Py, are utilized to reconstruct the buried SAM/perovskite interface. Both modifiers improve the wettability of the SAM surface and modulate the local interfacial environment via interactions with the SAM and perovskite components. Relative to FPA‐Ph, the extra pyridinic‐N sites in FPA‐Py further boost surface wettability and strengthen Pb 2+ coordination, concurrently generating a smoother and more homogeneous SAM layer. These synergistic effects promote the formation of compact perovskite films, favorable interfacial energetics, and optimized carrier dynamics. Consequently, FPA‐Py‐modified PSCs deliver a champion efficiency of 26.53% while possessing exceptional operational stability against high humidity, elevated temperature, and continuous illumination. This work demonstrates hydrophilization‐assisted molecular post‐treatment as an effective approach to buried‐interface reconstruction and provides rational molecular‐design guidance for the scalable fabrication of inverted PSCs.
papers.filename: Lili Ke, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Interfacial Hydrophilization-Assisted Buried-Interface Reconstruction for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Direct Optical Lithography of Intrinsically Stretchable Colloidal Emissive Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Abstract Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule crosslinker promotes efficient photopatterning, whereas the benzophenone-terminated polybutadiene crosslinker provides mechanical compliance. By tuning the crosslinker composition, the dual-crosslinking system enables direct optical patterning with line widths down to 2 μm and crack-free deformation up to 36% uniaxial strain. Both perovskite and InP-based nanocrystals largely retain their photoluminescence after processing, while the dual-crosslinking platform enables multicolor patterning and transfer to elastomeric substrates. QLEDs incorporating strained emissive layers maintain more than 90% of the maximum luminance of their unstretched counterparts. This dual-crosslinker design offers a general route to intrinsically stretchable, directly photopatternable colloidal nanocrystal emission layers.
papers.filename: Himchan Cho, Nano Lett., 2026, Direct Optical Lithography of Intrinsically Stretchable Colloidal Emissive Nanocrystals

papers.titleEn: Solvent Dipole Engineering Enables Large Quantum Dot Processing for Scalable Short-Wave Infrared Optoelectronics
papers.abstract: Abstract Semiconducting quantum dots (QDs) are key building blocks for optoelectronics, with tunable properties that depend on their size, shape, and surface chemistry. Large lead sulfide (PbS) QDs are particularly attractive for short-wave infrared (SWIR) optoelectronics, yet their processability is hindered by neutral facets, which compromise colloidal stability during liquid-phase ligand exchange and often lead to a collapse of the colloidal ink prior to processing. Herein, we demonstrate that solvent dipole engineering is an effective route for the scalable processing of large PbS QDs, eliminating the need for a layer-by-layer ligand exchange. The approach is utilized to fabricate SWIR-active photovoltaic diodes and photodetectors responsive over a broad spectral range, paving the way for their scalable production and commercialization.
papers.filename: Yana Vaynzof, ACS Energy Lett., 2026, Solvent Dipole Engineering Enables Large Quantum Dot Processing for Scalable Short-Wave Infrared Optoelectronics

papers.titleEn: Advanced Strategies of Self-Assembled Monolayers in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells: From Molecular Tailoring and Interfacial Engineering to Collective Dipole Modulation in Mixed Monolayers
papers.abstract: Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as critical hole transport materials (HTMs) for high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), owing to their ability to tailor surface energetics and buried interface chemistry. In this review, we summarize recent advances in SAM engineering for inverted PSCs, focusing on strategies in molecular design and interfacial modification and on emerging mixed SAM concepts. We discuss the structure–property relationships and molecular tailoring of SAM molecules, together with interfacial engineering at the buried interfaces for improving wettability and defect passivation to suppress nonradiative recombination. Particular attention is given to mixed SAM strategies. Despite rapid development of mixed SAM applications, rational guidelines for selecting and combining SAM molecules remain insufficiently established. Therefore, rather than relying on trial‐and‐error optimization, we propose collective dipole engineering as a rational framework for highest occupied molecular orbital level positioning to achieve improved charge carrier transport, without developing entirely new molecular systems. Overall, this review proposes dipole moment modulation as a key parameter linking interfacial chemistry with device physics for guiding selection of SAM combinations. Such collective dipole modulation provides a pathway toward highly efficient and operationally stable inverted PSCs, offering insights into the development of next‐generation HTMs in photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications.
